question: Did P9 variance-based conditional refinement actually accelerate the same P9 inference stream on the existing GPU in a repeatable manner with ≤1% prediction quality cost?
null: No consistent >=25% wall/GPU event reduction with ≤1% output MSE degradation across all three registered original P9 DEV seeds.

design.benchmark_device: existing CUDA 12.8 with torch 2.9.0+cu128 on isolated TTT GPU runner
design.paired_by: each of 24 randomized arm-order rounds, identical model weights and 64-event trace
design.CI: 2.5/97.5 percentile from 1000 deterministic bootstrap sample medians of paired per-round gated/dense ratios; no point omitted
design.metric_primary: host synchronized wall_ms; ratio of per-arm independent medians and 95% paired bootstrap upper-bound
design.metric_secondary: CUDA stream events elapsed ms; ratio of medians and 95% paired bootstrap upper-bound
design.accept_speed_and_quality: all three seed comparisons must individually have host and GPU event median ratio <=0.75, both paired bootstrap 95% upper ratio <=0.75, and variance-gate MSE <=1.01 dense MSE
design.gpu_event_caveat: measures stream interval between event records, includes Python kernel dispatch idle; does not isolate actual GPU occupancy/compute kernel cycles
